content.title: About
content.content: Almond milk is a plant‑based beverage made by blending almonds with water and straining the mixture. It has a mild nutty flavor, a light‑cream color, and is often used as a dairy‑free alternative.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Almond milk contains roughly 3‑5 times fewer calories than whole cow’s milk.
Commercial production of almond milk began in the United States in the 1990s.
In the U.S., almond milk has become the most popular plant milk, surpassing soy.
About 100 g of almonds are needed to produce 1 L of milk.
Almond milk is naturally lactose‑free, gluten‑free, and soy‑free.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that supports skin health and the immune system.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Unsweetened almond milk contains very little natural sugar, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Almonds provide monounsaturated fatty acids that help maintain cardiovascular health.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Fortified versions often contain calcium and vitamin D, nutrients essential for strong bones.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Being lactose‑free, it is safe for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to almonds may experience reactions when consuming almond milk.

items.title: Low protein content
items.content: Compared with cow’s milk, almond milk provides significantly less protein.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Flavored varieties can contain added sugars, increasing calorie count.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Almonds contain oxalates; people prone to kidney stones should limit intake.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Almond milk can be enjoyed on its own, added to coffee, smoothies, cereals, baked goods, or used in sauces. For a richer texture, choose unsweetened, full‑fat versions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store opened almond milk in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C and consume within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may separate.
